title: Everfield Clinic teletriage on-prem intake scratchpad
content:
TL;DR:
- Everfield Clinic is evaluating a private (on-prem/VPC) deployment of Redwood to power a 24/7 teletriage assistant that summarizes patient intake and suggests care pathways.
- Primary asks: PHI-safe pipeline, VPC-only networking, predictable p95 latency under 300ms for short triage replies, and local KMS/HSM for key material.
- PoC scope: 4-week technical validation focusing on connectivity, model performance with quantization, and data residency.

Attendees (2025-02-12 exploratory call):
- Dr. Anya Solano (Everfield product lead)
- Marco Hsu (Everfield infra lead)
- Priya Ramanathan (Redwood CS, owner)
- Omar Delgado (Redwood solutions eng)
- Lina Torres (Redwood security)

Background / motivation:
- Everfield runs regional clinics with strict PHI rules. They want to automate initial triage questions (symptoms, severity) and generate a short suggested care pathway (e.g., schedule nurse call, urgent ER referral).
- Current latency-sensitive path: clinicians want responses visible inside their EHR flow (Epic embed) within the intake workflow.
- Volume expectation: steady 5–8 req/s with peaks to ~22 req/s during morning shifts. Average prompt length small (patient 1–3 lines), but context window includes last 3 encounter notes (~1–1.5k tokens).

Requirements (functional / nonfunctional):
- PHI: all patient context stays inside customer network. No model or prompt telemetry leaves their VPC.
- Network: VPC peering from Redwood control plane -> customer-managed private control plane allowed? Everfield insists control plane metadata remain in their AWS account; they prefer a private control plane deployment.
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with YubiHSM / AWS CloudHSM. Keys used for model artifact encryption and TLS certs.
- Model: prefer an open LLM (Mistral/Redwood-verified variant) to avoid vendor model licensing, but will consider Redwood-managed variants if we can guarantee PHI isolation.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for single-turn triage replies, p99 < 700ms.
- Throughput: baseline 10 req/s with headroom to 25 req/s. Autoscaling windows need to be quick (scale up from idle GPU in <3min).
- Observability: token-level billing not important for PoC, but traces + per-request latency + model version tagged are required.
- Failover: local fallback policy to a smaller quantized model in case of capacity constraints; can tolerate graceful degradation but no silent data egress.

Constraints from Everfield infra (from Marco):
- On-prem cluster: 2 x NVIDIA A40 (shared across multiple internal teams).
- Strict egress rules: only outbound to a whitelisted Redwood control plane IP block via mTLS. No outbound to internet except for S3-compatible storage endpoint.
- DNS/proxy: corporate proxy is in the path for outbound; TLS interception is enforced for non-whitelisted destinations.
- Storage: artifacts should be pulled from their internal S3 (MinIO) with signed URLs; they prefer not to host scale-out NFS.

Potential implementation approaches (notes from solutions eng):
- Private control plane deployed in their AWS account + on-prem runtime connected via a peered VPC. Control plane handles job orchestration but model artifacts remain in their S3.
- Option B: fully air-gapped - Redwood provides an on-prem installer (VM/container bundle). Evaluate for later stage.
- Quantization: target int8 for performance; need to run offline eval to see accuracy drop on triage prompts (safety critical).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeated question patterns (same patient context), should reduce token generation overhead significantly during peak waves.

Gotchas / risks observed so far:
- Vendor telemetry: default telemetry will need toggling; customer requires opt-in explicit logging and retention policy. We must confirm our runtime does not attempt outbound calls for model validation or telemetry.
- TLS & mTLS handshake: corporate proxy occasionally rewrites SNI; we need to validate mTLS certs survive proxy.
- GPU availability: 2 A40s may be tight for peak with large models. Consider fallback to smaller model or batching policies with strict latency-aware routing.
- Model assembly time: cold-start (load model into GPU) measured at 60–90s for full FP16 model; with quantized int8 load ~30–40s. Need to document warm pool strategies.
- PHI-in-transit: the Epic integration team will want a signed data flow diagram for SOC/compliance review.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups):
- Which exact model family is approved by Everfield legal? (Dr. Solano to confirm internal list).
- Can they provide a dedicated GPU node for the PoC window? If not, what's acceptable degradation?
- Does their KMS deployment prefer CloudHSM or a Vault-backed HSM? Technical team to share architecture diagram (Marco).
- EHR integration pattern: do they want a synchronous REST call from the EHR or an async webhook + polling? (impact on latency SLOs).
- Logging retention: legal requires 90-day access audit logs for the PoC; confirm Redwood's plan for ephemeral logs in private control plane.

Notes from quick demo (2025-02-25 PoC kickoff):
- Ran a short live prompt set (5 common triage prompts): latency median ~180ms with int8 on a single A40, p95 ~320ms. Observed p95 slightly above target; batching and cache suggested to bring p95 down to ~260ms.
- Tokenization oddness: some triage templates truncated near 1k token context; need to add prompt preprocessing to compress encounter notes (extractive summary + bullets).
- Function-calling: they want structured output (triage_code, urgency_score, recommended_action) to map into Epic fields. We should prototype function schema and mapping.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- Marco (Everfield) to upload infra network diagram and HSM type into JIRA-2473 by 2025-02-18.
- Omar (Redwood) to run offline eval comparing FP16 vs int8 on customer triage prompt set; report accuracy delta and p95 numbers by 2025-02-21.
- Priya (me) to draft a minimal data flow diagram and privacy checklist for Everfield legal by 2025-02-20.
- Lina (Redwood security) to prepare a short runbook for enabling mTLS through corporate proxy and list required firewall rules by 2025-02-22.
- Schedule 1hr follow-up tech workshop (deep dive on model ops, caching) w/ Everfield infra + Epic integration team week of 2025-02-24.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Bring up quick prototype of extractive summarizer (2–3 sentence compress) to reduce context tokens. Could use cheap embedding+rank to pick salient sentences.
- Evaluate Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching window: try 10–20ms batching vs immediate; test impact on p95.
- Check if private control plane has a toggle to disable outbound DNS resolution (to satisfy their egress rules).

Misc raw fragments captured during call:
- "If it touches PHI, it stays on our network" (Anya)
- "We can't accept third-party key custody unless it's HSM-backed" (Marco)
- "Epic wants a JSON payload with urgency code mapped to triage workflows" (integration note)

Bottom line: good candidate for Private deployment PoC. Key blockers: explicit HSM/KMS agreement and resolving GPU capacity. Focus next week on offline eval and compliance diagram for legal.

-- end scratchpad --
